correctness.rationale: Direct angular differentiation proves all nonzero critical points have z^n real and excludes maxima on positive-power rays; each simple polynomial zero is a nondegenerate minimum. The radial stationarity polynomial Q(r^n)-n r^(n-2)Q'(r^n) has exactly 2k coefficient sign changes, so at most 2k positive roots counting multiplicity, and at most k maxima per negative-power ray. The origin is nondegenerate for n>=3. An explicit half-integer-scale placement forces 2k alternating signs when n>=ceil(8k log(8k)); hence the roots are simple and exactly kn+1 nondegenerate peaks occur. A standalone six-case rational checker replays; the universal proof is analytical.

value.rationale: The theorem determines a uniform sharp structural peak-count bound for natural finite-stellar-rank Husimi intensities with arbitrarily many concentric polygonal zero rings, and explicitly realizes all k simultaneous peak rings with a quantitative O(k log k) angular order sufficient threshold. This is a motivated all-parameter classification of the maximal possible count within the root-geometry family, not a finite small-degree table or a routine one-step increment. Exact minimal saturation order, saddle count and global peak competition are not claimed.
